high.title: Rate Cut Pressure May Dominate at July Monetary Policy Board Meeting
high.summary: The Bank of Korea's July Monetary Policy Board (MPB) meeting is shaping up to be a pivotal event, with analysts at Samsung Securities noting that even if the BOK proceeds with a base rate adjustment, the move may fail to act as a meaningful catalyst for higher bond yields. Researcher Kim Ji-man highlights that sharply falling oil prices and stabilizing core inflation are creating significant downward pressure on rates, suggesting the market is already leaning toward an easing bias. This is a critical signal for KRW and KTB (Korean Treasury Bond) traders: a dovish tilt — even within a nominally hawkish decision — could compress the short end of the yield curve while keeping long-dated yields anchored. For KRW, a more accommodative BOK stance relative to the Fed could widen the rate differential and sustain mild depreciation pressure on the Won. Investors should watch the MPB statement closely for dissenting votes and forward guidance language. Any hint of a prolonged easing cycle would be bullish for KTBs but bearish for KRW at the margin.

high.title: NDF at 1,498.00/1,498.40 Won — Down 1.95 Won
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month non-deliverable forward (NDF) settled below the psychologically significant 1,500 level in New York overnight, closing at a mid-rate of 1,498.20 won — a decline of 1.95 won from the previous Seoul spot close of 1,501.40 won. The bid/ask was quoted at 1,498.00/1,498.40, with the one-month swap point at -1.25 won factored into the calculation. The break below 1,500 in offshore NDF markets is a meaningful near-term signal for KRW bulls, suggesting that offshore participants are positioning for modest won appreciation heading into the Seoul open. This may reflect a combination of softer USD sentiment, risk-on flows, or pre-positioning ahead of next week's BOK MPB meeting and key data releases. Traders should monitor whether the Seoul onshore spot market confirms this move and sustains the sub-1,500 handle. A firm close below 1,500 in the onshore market would reinforce bullish KRW momentum, while a reversal back above that level would signal continued range-bound volatility.

high.title: [FX] Won Closes Below 1,500 Per Dollar on Yen Strength, Authorities' Vigilance
high.summary:
The USD/KRW exchange rate closed at 1,498.50 won at the end of the Seoul FX session on July 11th, a decline of 2.90 won from the previous day's 3:30 p.m. close of 1,501.40 won — and a notable 11.00 won drop compared to the prior day's 6 a.m. close of 1,509.50 won. The break back below the psychologically significant 1,500 level was driven by a combination of yen strength — which typically exerts sympathetic appreciation pressure across Asian currencies including the won — and continued vigilance from Korean FX authorities, suggesting potential verbal or active intervention posture. For KRW traders, the 1,500 level remains a critical threshold: a sustained close below this level could signal near-term bullish momentum for the won. Watch for whether yen strength persists and whether the BOK or Ministry of Economy and Finance escalate their intervention signals. The pace of won appreciation relative to regional peers will also be key for exporters' hedging behavior and capital flow dynamics in the coming sessions.

---

high.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] Back-to-Back Hikes, Terminal Rate in Focus as July BOK Meeting Looms
high.summary: South Korea's bond market is bracing for elevated volatility this week (July 13–16) with the Bank of Korea's July Monetary Policy Board meeting squarely in the crosshairs. A rate hike at the July 16 meeting is now widely treated as a done deal — which would mark the BOK's first tightening move in three and a half years, since January 2023, signaling a meaningful policy pivot. The critical market question is no longer whether the BOK hikes, but whether policymakers will signal consecutive rate increases and where the terminal rate ultimately lands. For KRW bond investors, the uncertainty around the hiking cycle's depth is the primary driver of yield volatility across the curve. A hawkish signal from Governor Rhee could steepen the short end aggressively, pressuring duration positions. Equity investors should also monitor spillover effects, as tighter financial conditions could weigh on rate-sensitive sectors. **Watch:** Forward guidance language in the BOK statement, any dissenting votes, and updated growth/inflation projections — these will be the key inputs for repricing both the front end and belly of the KTB curve this week.

high.title: [FX-Weekly] Won Eyes BOK Meeting, SK Hynix Dollar Inflows, Forward Sales
high.summary: The Seoul FX market is set for an eventful week (July 13–17), with USD/KRW having broken decisively below the psychologically significant 1,500 level last week for the first time in roughly six weeks — a development that opens the door to further KRW appreciation. Three key supply-demand dynamics are in focus: (1) **BOK Monetary Policy Board meeting** on July 16 — a rate hike would further support KRW by narrowing or reversing the Korea-U.S. rate differential, a longstanding headwind for the won; (2) **Dollar supply from SK Hynix** — corporate FX inflows from the semiconductor giant are expected to create meaningful USD selling pressure in the spot market, providing structural support for KRW; and (3) **Forward contract sales by heavy industry exporters** — these hedging flows represent additional USD supply, reinforcing the won's near-term bid. On the risk side, renewed U.S.-Iran military confrontation introduces geopolitical tail risk that could trigger risk-off flows and a sharp KRW reversal. **Watch:** The 1,480–1,490 range as the next technical support zone for USD/KRW; any escalation in Middle East tensions that could interrupt the current KRW strength trajectory.

high.title: New York FX Weekly Outlook: Yen Short Unwinding, US CPI/PPI in Focus, Hormuz Tensions Add Volatility
high.summary: Speculative yen net short positions are seeing their largest reduction in nearly two years, though the mechanics of Japan's repatriation plan — particularly how GPIF (Government Pension Investment Fund) intends to reallocate assets — remain ambiguous, leaving markets in a state of uncertainty. This week (July 13–17) will be pivotal for global FX dynamics, with the US CPI and PPI data releases and Federal Reserve Governor Warsh's congressional testimony serving as key inputs for July FOMC rate guidance.

medium.title: Financial Regulators' Weekly Schedule — July 13–19, 2026
medium.summary:
This is a high-density week for Korean macro data and policy events that traders must track closely. On Tuesday (July 14), the BOK will release International Financial and Foreign Exchange Market Trends for June 2026 — a key publication covering capital flows, FX reserve movements, and offshore KRW dynamics. Wednesday (July 15) brings the Export-Import Price Index and Trade Index (June preliminary) as well as May Money and Liquidity data, which will be closely watched for signs of credit growth trends and inflation pass-through. Most critically, Thursday (July 16) features the BOK Monetary Policy Board meeting at 09:00, followed by the Governor's press conference at 11:10 — the week's marquee event. The combination of FX flow data, trade pricing, and the rate decision in a single week creates elevated event risk for KRW, KTBs, and Korean equities. Fund managers should ensure positions are sized appropriately ahead of Thursday's decision.

---

medium.title: S. Korean Bond Futures Fall on Trump's 'Ceasefire Over' Remark — 10-Year Down 24 Ticks
medium.summary: South Korean government bond futures declined in overnight trading as geopolitical risk sentiment deteriorated following President Trump's statement that the ceasefire with Iran has ended. The 3-year bond futures closed at 103.07, down 3 ticks from the prior regular session close, while the 10-year futures fell a more significant 24 ticks — indicating greater sensitivity at the long end of the curve. Foreign investors were net buyers of 26 contracts in the 3-year segment, while financial investment firms and retail investors were net sellers, suggesting some divergence in domestic vs. foreign positioning. For KGB investors, the geopolitical flare-up introduces a risk-off dynamic that may temporarily pressure yields higher (prices lower), though the flight-to-safety narrative could reverse this depending on how the Iran situation evolves. Bond traders should monitor overnight U.S. Treasury moves and any BOK commentary as key directional cues.

medium.title: [New York Oil Price] 'Ceasefire Over' — Oil Falls Despite Trump Declaration, WTI Down 0.9%
medium.summary: WTI crude fell $0.67 (0.93%) to $71.41/barrel and Brent declined $0.29 (0.38%) to $76.01/barrel despite Trump's declaration that the ceasefire with Iran has ended, suggesting markets are skeptical of an immediate supply disruption. For Korea — a major oil importer — lower oil prices are directionally positive for the current account balance and help moderate imported inflation pressures, which in turn reduces urgency for BOK rate action. However, the geopolitical uncertainty around Iran warrants monitoring, as a sharp oil spike could quickly reverse these dynamics, widening Korea's import bill and adding upward pressure on CPI and the current account deficit.

medium.title: Korean Chip Stocks Test Limits of Rally Echoing Past Market Leaders
medium.summary:
The KOSPI has experienced sharp recent swings — falling 5.35% to 7,246.79 on July 8 before partially recovering to 7,291.91 (+0.62%) on July 9 — and the volatility is visibly reshaping investor behavior. Bargain hunters are pulling back from equities, with individual investors rotating into bank deposits and ultra-short-term products that offer absolute returns with lower risk. This shift is notable for KRW dynamics: a sustained equity market correction could dampen foreign investor appetite for Korean risk assets, potentially reducing equity-related capital inflows that have been a source of KRW support. The concurrent BOK rate hike cycle makes deposit products increasingly attractive relative to equities, reinforcing this rotation. **Implication:** Monitor foreign net buying/selling data on KOSPI closely this week, as sustained foreign outflows would be a headwind for KRW and could complicate the BOK's policy communication.

---

medium.title: Top 5 Financial Groups Provide ₩11.3 Trillion in Inclusive Finance in H1 — FSC to Launch Regular Monitoring
medium.summary:
South Korea's five major financial holding groups — KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, and NH NongHyup — collectively disbursed ₩11.3 trillion (~$9.5 billion) in inclusive finance products during the first half of 2025. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) announced plans to establish a formal, regular monitoring framework to track performance and ensure institutions treat inclusive finance as a structural ongoing obligation rather than a discretionary activity. This signals continued regulatory pressure on Korean banks to expand access to lower-income and underserved borrowers. For bond and equity investors in the banking sector, this introduces modest margin headwinds as banks may be steered toward lower-yield lending. It also reflects the FSC's broader macroprudential posture — worth monitoring as part of the overall credit expansion and household debt trajectory in Korea.

---

medium.title: US Military: Strait of Hormuz Open to All Vessels — Not Under Iranian Control
medium.summary:
US Central Command confirmed that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to international shipping, directly countering Iranian claims of control over the waterway. US forces stated they are deployed and ready to ensure freedom of navigation amid what they described as Iran's "unlawful attacks, harassment, and arbitrary declarations." While this statement is geopolitically stabilizing in tone, the underlying tensions signal continued risk to global energy supply routes. For Korean markets, this is materially relevant: Korea is heavily dependent on Middle East energy imports, and any sustained disruption to Hormuz transit would widen Korea's trade deficit, pressure the current account, and add inflationary impulses — all KRW-negative. Near-term resolution of headline risk may provide modest relief to oil prices, but traders should monitor escalation signals closely given Korea's structural energy import vulnerability.

---
